after.PASSED and VALIDATED: proposed to the owner as a paper strategy of its own (rule 14), on the US 500 CFD, about nine trades a year, sized by the risk engine, followed forward on paper; never real money
after.otherwise: reported as it is; nothing changes

spec.data: Yahoo daily closes: SPY adjusted for dividends and splits, ^IRX as published; each file's sha256 in the manifest; the computed calendar checked against the data's trading days

gates.beats_ordinary_days: event days beat every other day held the same way: mean difference > 0, Welch t >= 2.0
gates.costs_x2: mean net per event > 0 with the costs and the markup doubled
gates.t: t of the mean net return on event days, 1995..2021, >= the threshold
gates.top_year: no calendar year supplies more than 50% of the total net

spec.holdout_rule: 2022-01..2026-09: mean net per event > 0 with one-sided t >= 1.645, > 0 with the costs doubled, and above the ordinary days' mean
spec.holidays: NYSE scheduled full-day holidays by their rules: New Year's Day (not observed on a Friday), Martin Luther King Jr. Day from 1998, Washington's Birthday, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth from 2022, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas; Saturday holidays observed on Friday, Sunday ones on Monday
spec.question: does the S&P 500 earn a positive net return on the trading day before a market holiday, and more than on an ordinary day, after a CFD's costs?
